The Noble Qur'an, from the moment it was revealed, came accompanied by "In the name of Allah" (bism Allah), the Glorified and Exalted. Therefore, when we recite it, we begin with the same beginning that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, intended: that the beginning be "In the name of Allah."

The first words that the Revelation uttered to Muhammad (ﷺ) were: ﴿Read, in the name of your Lord who created﴾. Thus the beginning of the revelation of the Noble Qur'an, so that it might carry out its mission in the universe, was "In the name of Allah." And now, when we read the Qur'an, we begin with that same beginning.

Muhammad, peace be upon him, was in the Cave of Hira when Gabriel came to him, and the first meeting between the angel who carries the Revelation of the Qur'an and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was the saying of the Truth, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿Read﴾. "Read" requires that a person be either one who has memorized something, or have before him something written to read. But the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had not memorized anything to recite, and he did not have a book before him to read from. And even if he had had a book before him, he was unlettered, who could neither read nor write.

When Gabriel said, "Read," the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "I am not a reader." The Messenger (ﷺ) was being logical in line with his abilities. The words were repeated three times: Gabriel, peace be upon him, by inspiration from Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, says to the Messenger, "Read," and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) says, "I am not a reader." The enemies of Islam seized upon this point and said: how does Allah tell His Messenger "Read," and the Messenger replies, "I am not a reader"?

We say: Allah, Blessed and Exalted, was speaking through His power, which says to a thing "Be," and it is; while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was speaking through his humanity, which says that he cannot read a single word. But the power of Allah is what would take this Prophet, who neither reads nor writes, and make him a teacher for all of humanity until the Day of Resurrection, because all people are taught by humans, but Muhammad (ﷺ) would be taught by Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, so that he would be a teacher to the greatest scholars of mankind, who take knowledge and understanding from him. Therefore the answer came from Allah, the Glorified and Exalted:

﴿Read in the name of your Lord who created. He created man from a clinging substance. Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous﴾ (Surat al-'Alaq).

That is, Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, who created from nothing, will make you recite to the people what the scholars of the world and the civilizations of the world are unable to produce the like of. What you recite, though you are the unlettered Prophet, will be a miracle, not only for those who hear it from you at the moment of its descent, but for the whole world, and not only at the time it is revealed, but until the Hour arrives. That is why the One of majestic glory said:

﴿Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous, who taught by the pen﴾ (Surat al-'Alaq).

That is, what you will recite, O Muhammad, will remain a teacher of all humanity until the end of the world on earth. And because the Teacher is Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, He said, ﴿Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous﴾, using the intensive form. For there is "generous" and "most generous." When you learn from a human being, this is evidence of the generosity of Allah, majestic in glory, because He facilitated knowledge for you through the hand of a human like yourself. But if Allah is the One who teaches you, that is "most generous," because your Lord has raised you to a high rank so that He, the Glorified and Exalted, might teach you Himself.

The Truth wants to draw our attention to the fact that Muhammad (ﷺ) does not read the Qur'an because he learned reading, but he reads it "in the name of Allah," and as long as it is in the name of Allah, it does not matter whether the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) learned from a human being or did not learn. For the One who taught him is Allah, and his knowledge is above the level of all humanity.

Moreover, we also begin the recitation of the Qur'an in the name of Allah, because Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is the One who sent it down to us and facilitated for us to know it and recite it. So the matter belongs to Allah in knowledge, power and understanding. Read the saying of the Truth, the Glorified and Exalted:

﴿Say: If Allah had willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made it known to you. Indeed I remained among you a lifetime before it. Will you not then reason?﴾ (Surat Yunus).

Therefore you recite the Qur'an in the name of Allah, because He, majestic in glory, is the One who facilitated it for you as speech, revelation and recitation. But are we required to begin only the recitation of the Qur'an with "In the name of Allah"? We are required to begin every work with "In the name of Allah," because we must honor Allah's bounty in His universe. For example, when we plough the land, we must begin with "In the name of Allah," because we did not create the land we plough, nor did we create the seed we sow, nor did we send down the water from the sky for the crop to grow.

The farmer who grasps the hoe and casts the seed may be the most ignorant of people about the elements of the soil, the contents of the seed, and what water does in the earth for the crop to grow. All that man does is apply the mind created by Allah to the matter created by Allah, with the energy Allah placed in our bodies, so that the planting may be completed.

Man has no ability to force the earth to give him fruit, nor any ability to create the grain so that it grows and becomes a tree, nor any authority to bring down water from the sky. So when he begins the work with "In the name of Allah," it is as if he begins with the name of the One who subjected the earth to him, subjected the grain to him, and subjected the water to him, all of which he has no power over and which are not within his capacity or ability. It is as if he declares that he enters upon all these things by the name of the One who subjected them to him.

Allah, Blessed and Exalted, subjected the whole universe to us and gave us the proof of that. So do not think that you have power or independent existence in this universe, and do not think that the causes and laws in the universe have independent existence. Rather, they operate by the power of their Creator, who, if He wills, causes them to operate, and if He wills, halts them.

The huge camel and the immense tame elephant may be led by a small child, and they obey him. But the small snake cannot be tamed by any human being. Had we been doing this by our own powers, taming a snake or a serpent would have been easy because of their small size. But Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, wanted to make them an example, so that we would know that by His power He has subjected to us what He willed, and has not subjected to us what He willed. Therefore the Truth, Blessed and Exalted, says:

﴿Do they not see that We created for them, from what Our hands have made, livestock, and they are their owners? And We subjected them to them, so some of them they ride and some of them they eat﴾ (Surat Ya-Sin).

Thus we know that the submission of these livestock to us is by Allah's subjecting them, not by our power.

Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, comes to a land on which rain falls abundantly. The scientists say that this happens through the laws of the universe. So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, draws our attention to the error of this statement, by bringing seasons of drought in which not a single drop of rain falls, so that we know that rain does not fall by the laws of the universe but by the will of the Creator of the universe. For if the laws alone were operating, who then halted them? But the will of the Creator is above the laws: if He wills, He makes them operate, and if He wills, He makes them not operate. So everything in the universe is in the name of Allah; He is the One who subjects and gives, and He is the One who grants and withholds, even in matters where a human has some degree of choice. Read the saying of the Truth, Blessed and Exalted:

﴿To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He creates what He wills. He bestows female [offspring] upon whom He wills and bestows male [offspring] upon whom He wills, or He pairs them, males and females, and He renders whom He wills barren. Indeed He is Knowing and Competent﴾ (Surat ash-Shura).

The basic principle regarding offspring is that they come from the union of a male and a female; this is the law. But laws operate only by the command of Allah. Thus a man and a woman marry and no offspring comes, because it is not the law that creates; rather, it is the will of the Creator of the law. If He wills, He makes it operate, and if He wills, He nullifies its operation. Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, is not governed by laws; rather, He is the One who governs them.

Just as Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, is able to make the laws act or not act, so He is able to break the laws. Take as an example the story of Zachariah, peace be upon him. He was the guardian of Mary, and he would bring her everything she needed. He entered upon her and found with her what he had not brought her.

He asked her, and she was the devout worshipper who kept constantly to her sanctuary: ﴿He said, "O Mary, from where is this for you?"﴾ (Surat Al 'Imran).

The Truth, Blessed and Exalted, gives us this picture, although Mary, by her conduct, worship and piety, was above all suspicion. But so that we know that what corrupts the universe is the failure to ask about the source of things that do not match the capacities of the one who obtains them.

The mother sees the father spending beyond what his salary allows, and sees the daughter wearing far more than her income or allowance. If the mother or the father or the daughter were asked, "From where is this for you?", society would not be corrupted. But corruption comes from our closing our eyes to unlawful wealth.

How did Mary, peace be upon her, reply?

﴿She said, "It is from Allah. Indeed, Allah provides for whom He wills without account"﴾ (Surat Al 'Imran).

Thus the absoluteness of Allah's power is not governed by any law. Mary drew Zachariah, peace be upon them both, to the absoluteness of power. So Zachariah called upon his Lord in a matter in which only the absoluteness of power is of any use: he was an old man, and his wife was old and barren, and he wanted a son. This is a matter against the laws of the universe, for procreation occurs only in youth; when the man grows old and the woman grows old, they do not bear children. How much more so when the wife was essentially barren, who did not bear children while she was young and her husband was young? How then would she bear children while she is old and her husband is old? This is a matter against the laws that govern humans. But Allah alone is able to bring about the law and its opposite. Therefore He willed to grant Zachariah a child, and it was; and Zachariah was granted his son, Yahya.

So everything in this universe is in the name of Allah, happens in the name of Allah and by the permission of Allah. The universe is governed by causes, yes; but the will of Allah is above all causes.

When you begin everything with "In the name of Allah," it is as if you make Allah your helper on your side. And by the mercy of Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, He taught us to begin everything with "In the name of Allah," because Allah is the all-comprehensive Name that gathers the attributes of perfection, the Glorified and Exalted. An action generally requires multiple attributes. So when you begin a work you need the power of Allah, His help and His mercy. Had Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, not told us of the all-comprehensive Name that gathers all the attributes, we would have had to specify the attributes we need, saying, "In the name of Allah the Strong," "In the name of Allah the Provider," "In the name of Allah the Responsive," "In the name of Allah the Capable," "In the name of Allah the Beneficial," and so on through the other names and attributes by which we wish to seek help. But Allah, Blessed and Exalted, made us say: "In the name of Allah, in the name of Allah, in the name of Allah," the One who gathers all these attributes.

We must pause here at those who do not begin their works with "In the name of Allah," and seek only material reward. A disbelieving person does not begin his work with "In the name of Allah," and a believing person begins every work with Allah in mind. Both receive from the world, because Allah is the Lord of all. He has the gift of lordship for all His creatures whom He summoned to life. But the world is not the true life of the human being; rather, the true life is the Hereafter. The one whose mind holds only this world takes according to the measure of the gift of lordship, according to the measure of Allah's gift in this world. And the one whose mind holds Allah takes according to the measure of Allah's gift in this world and the Hereafter. Therefore the Truth, Blessed and Exalted, says: ﴿Praise be to Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and to Him belongs praise in the Hereafter, and He is the Wise, the Acquainted﴾ (Surat Saba, 34:1). For the believer praises Allah for His blessings in this world, then praises Him when He saves him from the Fire and punishment and admits him to Paradise in the Hereafter. So praise is to Allah in this world and the Hereafter.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Every important matter that does not begin with 'In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful' is cut off." (1)

Meaning of "cut off" (abqa'): that is, having a cut tail or hem, i.e., an incomplete work in which something is lost; for when you do not begin the work with "In the name of Allah," pride and transgression may befall you...

1 Narrated by al-Suyuti in al-Jami' al-Saghir, attributing it to 'Abd al-Qadir al-Rahawi at the beginning of the book "al-Arba'in," from Abu Hurayrah, with a sound chain (isnad hasan); and Ibn Kathir narrated it in his tafsir with the wording "then it is ajdham."

When we move on to His saying, exalted is He, ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾, Allah is praised for His essence, praised for His attributes, praised for His blessings, praised for His mercy, praised for His way (manhaj), praised for His decree. Allah is praised before He created anyone who would praise Him. It is among the mercies of Allah, glorified and exalted is He, that He made thanks to Him to lie in two words: al-Hamdu lillah (Praise be to Allah).

What is remarkable is that when you thank a human being for a good deed, you keep going for hours. You count the words of thanks and praise, you delete and add, and you take the opinions of people, until you arrive at a poem or a speech full of praise and gratitude. But Allah, glorified is His power and great is His majesty, His blessings cannot be counted or enumerated, and He taught us to thank Him in two words: al-Hamdu lillah.

Perhaps we can understand that excessive thanks to people is disliked, because it afflicts a person with conceit and hypocrisy and increases the disobedient in his disobedience. So let us minimize thanks and praise to people, for we thank Allah for His great blessings upon us with two words: al-Hamdu lillah. It is among the mercies of Allah, glorified and exalted is He, that He taught us the formula of praise. For if He had left it without specifying it in two words, it would have been difficult for people to find the appropriate formula to praise Allah for this divine perfection. Whatever eloquence and ability to express people are given, they are unable to reach a formula of praise worthy of the majesty of the Benefactor. How, then, can we praise Allah when the intellect is unable to grasp His power, enumerate His blessings, or encompass His mercy? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave us an image of human inability to praise the perfection of Divinity, when he said: "I cannot enumerate praise of You; You are as You have praised Yourself."

And the two words al-Hamdu lillah, through them Allah made all people equal. For if He had left praise without specification, the degrees of praise would have varied among people according to their varying abilities of expression. This one is unlettered, who neither reads nor writes, and cannot find the words with which to praise Allah. And this scholar has the ability to express and can produce the formula of praise with what he has been given of knowledge and eloquence. Thus the degrees of people in praise vary, according to their positions in this worldly life.

But the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, willed in His justice to make His servants equal in the formula of praise to Him. So He teaches us, in the first of His words in the Noble Qur'an, that we should say "al-Hamdu lillah", to give equal opportunity to all His servants, such that the learned and the unlearned are equal in the giving of praise, and whoever has been given eloquence and whoever cannot speak well.

Therefore we praise Allah, glorified and exalted is He, for having taught us how to praise Him, so that the servant may always be praising and Allah may always be praised. Allah, glorified and exalted is He, before creating us, created for us the causes of praise in the form of blessings. He created for us the heavens and the earth, brought into being for us water and air, and placed in the earth its sustenance until the Day of Resurrection. This is a blessing for which He deserves praise, because He, majestic is His majesty, made blessing precede human existence. When man was created, blessing was already present to receive him. Indeed, before Allah, majestic is His majesty, created Adam, father of all mankind, the Garden in which he lived preceded him, where he did not toil nor suffer. He was created and found what he eats, what he drinks, what sustains his life, and what he enjoys existing, ready and prepared before creation. And when Adam and Eve descended to the earth, blessing had preceded them. They found what they would eat and drink, and what would sustain their lives. And if blessing had not preceded human existence, but had been created after it, man would have perished while waiting for the coming of blessing.

Moreover, divine giving to man gives him blessing the moment he is created in his mother's womb. He finds a womb prepared to receive him and nourishment sufficient for him throughout the period of pregnancy. When he comes out into this world, Allah places in his mother's breast milk that descends when he is hungry and withholds when he is satisfied. It ends completely when the period of nursing stops. He finds a father and a mother who provide for him the necessities of his life until he can support himself. All this happens before a person reaches the stage of accountability (taklif) and before he can utter: "al-Hamdu lillah."

Thus we see that blessing always precedes the one who receives it. So when a person says "al-Hamdu lillah," it is because the causes of praise, which are blessings, exist in the universe before human existence.

Allah, glorified and exalted is He, created for us in this universe things that give man without any ability on his part and without his submission to them, while man is unable to provide himself with these blessings which the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, gives him without effort. The sun gives warmth and life to the earth without payment and without any action by humans. The rain falls from the sky without you having any effort in it or ability to send it down. The air is around you everywhere, and you breathe from it without effort or ability on your part. The earth gives you fruit merely when you scatter the seed in it and water it. The crop grows by the power of Allah. The night and day alternate so that you may sleep to rest, and strive for your life. You did not bring the light of day, nor did you create the darkness of night, but you take rest at night and work by day, by the power of Allah, without doing anything.

None of these things did man create, but he was created to find them in the universe giving him without payment and without effort on his part. Does this not deserve that we say praise for the blessing of subjecting the universe to the service of man? It requires that praise be due.

And the signs of Allah, glorified and exalted is He, in His universe demand praise.

The life which Allah bestowed upon us, and the signs He deposited in His universe to guide us to the fact that this universe has a great Creator.

The universe, with its sun, moon, stars, earth, and all that is in it, exceeds the capacity of man, and no one can claim it for himself. No one, however great his knowledge, can claim that he created the sun, brought the stars into being, placed the earth, set the laws of the universe, gave its atmosphere, or created himself or created others.

All these signs have given us evidence of the existence of a supreme power, which brought into being and created. These signs are not still, so that by their stillness we would forget them; rather they are in motion to turn us toward the Creator of this great universe.

The sun rises in the morning to remind us of the miracle of creation, and sets in the evening to remind us of the greatness of the Creator. The alternation of night and day occurs before us every day, so that perhaps we will turn and awaken. The rain falls from the sky to remind us of the divinity of the One who sent it down. The crop comes out of the earth, watered by one water, yet each kind has its color, its shape, its taste, its smell, and its own constitution differing from the other. Then comes the harvest, and the fruit and crop disappear, and the season of planting comes and it returns anew.

Everything in this universe is in motion to remind us when we forget, and to teach us that there is a great Creator.

We could go on in this without end, for the blessings of Allah cannot be counted or enumerated. Each one of them guides us to the existence of the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, and gives us the evidence of faith that this universe has a creative Creator. And that no one can claim that he created the universe or created anything in it. The matter is settled for Allah. And "al-Hamdu lillah," because He placed in our souls innate faith, then reinforced it with rational faith through His signs in His universe.

Indeed everything in this universe demands praise, yet man praises the existent and forgets the Existent!! When you see a beautiful jewel, for example, or a flower exceeding in its beauty, or any creation of Allah's creation, beauty pervades your soul and you praise this creation, saying: "How beautiful this flower is," or "this jewel," or "this creature." But the creature you praised did not give itself the attribute of beauty. The flower has no part in being beautiful or not beautiful, and the jewel has no part in the greatness of its creation. Everything in this universe did not place beauty in itself, rather the One who placed beauty in it is Allah, glorified and exalted is He. So let us not confuse matters and praise the creature while forgetting the Creator. Rather say: "Praise be to Allah who placed in the universe what reminds us of the greatness of the Creator and the precision of creation."

The method of Allah, glorified and exalted is He, requires praise from us, because Allah sent down His way to show us the path of good and keep us away from the path of evil.

The way of Allah which He sent down upon His messengers has made known to us that Allah, blessed and exalted is He, is the One who created this universe and created us. The precision and greatness of creation indicate to us that there is a great Creator. But they cannot tell us who He is, nor what He wants from us. For this reason Allah sent His messengers, to tell us: the One who created this universe and created us is Allah, blessed and exalted is He, and this requires praise.

The way of Allah has made clear to us what the Truth wants from us, and how to worship Him. This requires praise. The way of Allah, majestic is His majesty, has given us the path and legislated for us the style of our life, legislation in truth. Allah, blessed and exalted is He, does not distinguish between any of us, nor prefer one over another except by piety; all of us are created equal before Allah, majestic is His majesty.

So: the legislation of truth, the word of truth, and the judgment of truth come from Allah. As for human legislations, they have desires, distinguishing some from others, taking the rights of some to give to others. For this reason you find in every human system injustice committed by humans. In the communist states, the members of the central committee are the people of blessing and luxury, while the whole people are in misery, because those who legislated followed their own desires and placed their interests above every interest. And likewise in capitalist states, the owners of capital take all the good.

But Allah, glorified and exalted is He, when He sent down the way to us, decreed justice among people and gave every rightful person his right. He taught us how life is set right on earth when it is far from human desire and subject to the justice of Allah, and this requires praise.

The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, deserves praise from us, because He does not take from us but gives us. Humans in every age try to exploit humans, because they covet what is in their hands of wealth and money. But Allah, glorified and exalted is He, does not need what is in our hands. He gives us and does not take from us; with Him are the treasuries of everything, in confirmation of His saying, majestic is His majesty: ﴿And there is not a thing but that with Us are its treasuries, and We do not send it down except in a known measure﴾ [21]

(Surat al-Hijr).

So Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is constantly giving to His creation, and creation constantly takes from the blessings of Allah. It is as if servanthood to Allah gives you and takes nothing from you, and this requires praise.

And Allah, glorified and exalted is He, in His giving, loves to be asked by man, to be called upon, and to be sought for help. This requires praise, because it protects us from humiliation in this world. For if you ask something from a man of influence, he must set for you an appointment or a time for conversation and a duration for the meeting, and he may become impatient with you and stand up to end the meeting. But the door of Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is always open. You are before Him whenever you wish, and you raise your hands to heaven and call upon Him whenever you love, and ask Allah for whatever you want, and He gives you what you want if it is good for you, and withholds from you what you want if it is evil for you.

Allah, glorified and exalted is He, asks you to call upon Him and to ask Him, saying:

﴿And your Lord says: Call upon Me, I will respond to you. Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me will enter Hell, humiliated﴾ [60] (Surat Ghafir).

And He, glorified and exalted is He, says:

﴿And when My servants ask you about Me, indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me. So let them respond to Me and believe in Me that they may be guided﴾ [186] (Surat al-Baqarah).

And Allah, glorified and exalted is He, knows what is in your soul, and therefore He gives you without your asking. Read the sacred hadith:

The Lord of Might says: "Whoever is preoccupied with remembering Me instead of asking Me, I will give him the best of what I give those who ask" (1). And the giving of Allah, glorified and exalted is He, does not run out, and His treasuries do not empty. Whenever you ask Him, majestic is His majesty, He has more. Whatever you ask Him, nothing is too difficult for Allah, glorified and exalted is He, if He wills to bring it about for you.

And read the saying of the poet:

Sufficient for my self honor that I am His servant,
He welcomes me without appointments, my Lord,
And He, in His holiness, the Most Mighty, but
I meet whenever I...

(1) Narrated by al-Bukhari, al-Bazzar and al-Bayhaqi from Ibn Umar.

Now, when we move to His saying, the Exalted: ﴿The Most Gracious, the Most Merciful﴾, then among the things that necessitate praise is that Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, is Most Gracious and Most Merciful. He gives His blessings in this world to all His servants, a gift of lordship (ʿaṭāʾ rubūbiyyah), and the gift of lordship is for both the believer and the disbeliever. The gift of lordship does not cease except when a person dies.

Allah does not withhold His blessings from His servants in this world. The blessings of Allah cannot be counted or enumerated, and despite all the advances in calculating machines, electronic brains and other such things, we have not found anyone who steps forward and says, "I will count the blessings of Allah." This is because the requirement for counting is that you be capable of it. You do not undertake to count anything unless you have the ability to enumerate it. But since that is beyond your capacity and power, you do not undertake it. For this reason, no one will come forward on the Day of Resurrection to count the blessings of Allah, blessed and exalted, because no one can enumerate them. We must also note that the whole universe is constricted by man, and that the subjugated world which serves us by the rule of compulsion and subjection becomes constricted when it sees the disobedient, because what is subjugated is upright upon the way of Allah by compulsion. So when every subjugated thing sees a man who is its servant disobeying, it becomes constricted.

And read the ḥadīth qudsī so that you may know something of the mercy of Allah toward His servants. The Mighty and Majestic says:

"There is no day on which its sun rises but the sky calls out, saying: 'O Lord, permit me to drop fragments upon the son of Adam, for he has eaten of Your provision and withheld thanks to You.' And the seas say: 'O Lord, permit me to drown the son of Adam, for he has eaten of Your provision and withheld thanks to You.' And the mountains say: 'O Lord, permit me to crush the son of Adam, for he has eaten of Your provision and withheld thanks to You.' Then Allah, exalted, says: 'Leave them, leave them. If you had created them, you would have shown them mercy. They are My servants. If they turn in repentance to Me, I am their beloved, and if they do not repent, I am their physician.'" Related by Imam Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal in his Musnad.

These are the manifestations of the attributes ar-Raḥmān and ar-Raḥīm, and how He guaranteed us the continuance of everything that serves us in this universe despite human disobedience. All of it serves us by the gift of lordship and continues in our service by Allah's subjugation of it, because He is Most Gracious and Most Merciful.

Some people may ask: do the earth, the heavens and other creatures in the realms of inanimate things, plants and animals speak? We say yes. They have a language which we do not know; only their Creator knows it. The proof is that from the very first creation, the Truth, blessed and exalted, informed us that there is a language for all these creatures. Read His saying, Majestic is His majesty:

﴿Then He turned to the heaven when it was smoke, and said to it and to the earth: "Come both of you, willingly or unwillingly." They said: "We come willingly."﴾ (Surah Fussilat, 41:11).

So the earth and the heavens understood from Allah, and they said to Him, glory be to Him and exalted, ﴿We come willingly﴾. Did not Allah teach Solomon the speech of birds and the language of the ant? Did the mountains not glorify Allah along with David? Thus every creation of Allah has perceptions suited to it, indeed it has feelings.

When Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, spoke about the people of Pharaoh, He said:

﴿How many gardens and springs they left behind, and crops and a noble station, and comfort in which they took delight. Thus it was, and We bequeathed them to another people. So the heaven and the earth did not weep for them, nor were they reprieved.﴾ (Surah ad-Dukhan, 44:25–29).

So the heavens and the earth have response, a response that reaches the stage of weeping. They did not weep over Pharaoh and his people, but they weep in sorrow when a believing man who prays and adheres to the way of Allah departs from them. Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "When a believer dies, two places weep for him: a place on earth and a place in the heaven. As for the place on earth, it is the place of his prayer that made him happy when he prayed in it. As for the place in the heaven, it is the ascent of his good deeds."

If all of God's blessings deserve praise, then ﴿Master of the Day of Judgment﴾ deserves great praise, because if there were no day of reckoning, the one who filled the world with evil would escape without being requited for what he did. And the one who committed himself to the obligations and worship and deprived himself of many worldly pleasures in pleasing God would have been miserable in this worldly life. But because God, blessed and exalted is He, is ﴿Master of the Day of Judgment﴾, He has given balance to all existence. This sovereignty over the Day of Judgment is what protected the weak and the oppressed and kept justice in God's universe. What prevented the world from turning into a jungle, where the strong devour the weak and the oppressor preys on the oppressed, is that there is an Hereafter and a reckoning, and that God, glorified and exalted is He, is the One who will call His creation to account.

The upright person's uprightness benefits others, because he fears God, gives every person his due right, pardons and forgives. Thus everyone around him benefits from his noble character and from his standing with truth and justice.

As for the disobedient person, society suffers because of him, since no one is safe from his evil and no one escapes his injustice. Therefore ﴿Master of the Day of Judgment﴾ is the scale. You know that the one who corrupts the earth awaits the Hereafter. He will not escape, however great his strength and influence, so you are completely reassured that God's justice will overtake every oppressor.

Moreover, ﴿Master of the Day of Judgment﴾ has two recitations: ﴿مالك يوم الدين﴾ and ملك يوم الدين (Malik). Both recitations are sound. God, blessed and exalted is He, described Himself in the Noble Qur'an as ﴿Master of the Day of Judgment﴾. The master (مالك) of a thing is the one who alone disposes of it; no other individual has any say in it. I own my cloak, I own my belongings, I own my house, and I am the one who disposes of all of this, judging concerning it as I see fit.

So ﴿Master of the Day of Judgment﴾ means that God, glorified and exalted is He, will direct the affairs of the servants on that day without intermediary causes, and that everything will come directly from God, with no one able to intervene, even outwardly.

In this world God gives sovereignty outwardly to some people, but on the Day of Resurrection there is no outward appearance; the command is direct from God, glorified and exalted is He. Therefore God says, describing the Day of Judgment:

﴿Nay, but you deny the Judgment﴾ (Surah al-Infitar, 9).

It is as though God created man in this world so that life might proceed through him, but in the Hereafter there are no intermediary causes. Sovereignty in the outward affairs of this world is from God, Who bestows it on whom He wills. Read His saying, exalted is He:

﴿Say: "O God, Master of sovereignty, You give sovereignty to whom You will, and You strip sovereignty from whom You will, and You exalt whom You will, and You abase whom You will; in Your hand is good. Indeed You are over all things competent."﴾ (Surah Al 'Imran, 26).

Perhaps His saying ﴿You strip﴾ (tanzi'u) draws our attention to the fact that no one in this world wants to give up sovereignty, but sovereignty must be wrested from him by force against his will. It is God who strips sovereignty from whom He wills.

Here we ask: is sovereignty in this world and the Hereafter not God's? We say the matter at every moment belongs to God. But God, blessed and exalted is He, has made some of His creatures vicegerents or empowered them with sovereignty on earth. Therefore in the Noble Qur'an we find His saying:

﴿Have you not considered the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord, because God had given him sovereignty? When Abraham said, "My Lord is He who gives life and causes death," he said, "I give life and cause death." Abraham said, "Indeed God brings the sun from the east, so bring it from the west." So the one who disbelieved was confounded. And God does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 258).

The one who argued with Abraham concerning his Lord was a disbeliever who denied divinity. Yet he did not take sovereignty by his own essence; rather God, majestic is His majesty, gave him sovereignty. So God, blessed and exalted is He, is the One who made some of His creatures vicegerents and empowered them over the land of the earth outwardly. This means that it is an outward sovereignty over people only: a human being becomes a king, but sovereignty does not emanate from the essence of the one who holds it; it emanates from God's command. Had it emanated from the self of the one who holds it, it would have remained with him and not been taken from him. Outward sovereignty is a test for the servants, and God will call them to account on the Day of Resurrection: how did they conduct themselves, and what did they do? And people are tested by it: did they remain silent before the unjust ruler, did they prefer disobedience, or did they stand with truth against oppression? God, glorified and exalted is He, does not test people in order to know the reformer from the corrupter; rather He tests them so that they become witnesses against themselves, lest one of them come on the Day of Resurrection and say, "O Lord, if You had given me sovereignty, I would have followed the path of truth and applied Your method."

Here a question arises: if God, glorified and exalted is He, knows everything, why the test? We say that when we want to give an example that brings this closer to minds, and to God belongs the highest example, we find that universities throughout the world hold examinations for their students. Do the university professors who taught these students not know what the student knows, and do they want to obtain knowledge from him? Of course not. But this happens so that when the student fails the examination and comes to argue, they confront him with his answer and he falls silent. Had the examination not been held, every student would have claimed that he deserves a place of honour.

When the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, says ﴿Master of the Day of Judgment﴾, that is, the One who alone owns that day and disposes of it as He wills. And when it is said ﴿Master of the Day of Judgment﴾, His disposal is higher than that of the owner, because the owner disposes only of his own property, whereas the sovereign disposes of his own property and the property of others, so he can issue laws for confiscating or nationalizing what others own.

Those who recite ﴿Master of the Day of Judgment﴾ establish for God, glorified and exalted is He, that He is the Master of that day, disposing of it as He wills without intervention from anyone, even outwardly. Those who recite Malik say that God, glorified and exalted is He, on that day judges the affairs of His creatures, including those whom He had given outward sovereignty in this world. We say that when the Day of Resurrection comes, there is no master and no sovereign except God.

God, blessed and exalted is He, wants to reassure His servants: that if they have been afflicted with a master or sovereign who oppresses them, then on the Day of Resurrection there is no master and no sovereign except God, majestic is His majesty. When you say Master or Sovereign of the Day of Judgment, there is a day and there is the Judgment. The day, for us, is from sunrise to sunrise; this is what we call a day. In its meaning, the day is a time-frame in which events occur. The commentators say ﴿Master of the Day of Judgment﴾ means Master of the affairs of the Judgment, because a time-frame cannot be owned. We say that this is by the measures of human ownership, for we do not own time: we cannot bring back the past, nor can we bring about the future. But God, blessed and exalted is He, is the Creator of time, and God, majestic is His majesty, is not confined by time or place. Likewise His saying ﴿Master of the Day of Judgment﴾ is not confined by time or place. Read His saying, glorified is He:

﴿And they ask you to hasten the punishment, but God will not fail His promise. Indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count.﴾ (Surah al-Hajj, 47).

And His saying, exalted is He:

﴿The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him in a day whose measure is fifty thousand years.﴾ (Surah al-Ma'arij, 4).

If we reflect on these two verses, we know the meaning of the day with God, blessed and exalted is He. God, majestic is His majesty, is the Creator of time, and therefore He can create a day whose measure is an hour, a day like the days of this world whose measure is twenty-four hours, a day whose measure is a thousand years, a day whose measure is fifty thousand years, and a day whose measure is a million years. That is subject to God's will.

The Day of Judgment exists in God's knowledge, glorified and exalted is He, with all its events, its Paradise and its Fire, and all the creatures who will be reckoned on it. When He wills that this day come into being and pass from His knowledge, majestic is His majesty, into the knowledge of His creatures, whether they be angels, humans or jinn, He says: "Be," and it is. God alone is the Creator of this day, and He alone determines all its dimensions. We outwardly define the day as twenty-four hours, and we define it as night and day. But the truth is that night and day exist constantly on the earth. When the earth moves, every movement is the end of a day in one region and the beginning of a day in another, the beginning of a night in one region and the end of a night in another. Therefore at every moment one day ends and another begins. Thus, if you take the terrestrial globe with a comprehensive view, day never ends upon it, and night never ends upon it. So the day is relative to every spot on the earth, yet in reality it is constantly present across the whole globe.

God, glorified and exalted is He, wants to reassure His servants: that if injustice befalls them in this world, there is a day in which there is no injustice, and on that day the matter belongs to God alone, without intermediary causes. Every person whom justice and retribution do not overtake in this world, the Hereafter awaits him. And the one who followed God's method and restrained his movement in life, God, glorified and exalted is He, informs him that there is a day on which he will receive his reward. The greatness of the Hereafter is that it gives you Paradise: a bliss that will not escape you, nor you it.

One of the men entered upon a righteous man and said, "I want to know: am I among the people of this world or among the people of the Hereafter?" The righteous man said to him, "God is more merciful to His servants, so He has not placed their scales in the hands of their like. Each person's scale is in his own hand. Why? Because you can deceive people, but you cannot deceive yourself. Your scale is in your hands. You can know whether you are among the people of this world or among the people of the Hereafter."

The man said, "How is that?" The righteous servant replied: "If someone comes in to you who gives you money, and someone comes in to you who takes charity from you, which of them do you rejoice at?" The man was silent. The righteous servant said: "If you rejoice at the one who gives you money, you are among the people of this world. If you rejoice at the one who takes charity from you, you are among the people of the Hereafter. For a person rejoices at the one who presents to him what he loves. The one who gives me money gives me this world, and the one who takes charity from me gives me the Hereafter. So if you are among the people of the Hereafter, rejoice at the one who takes charity from you more than your rejoicing at the one who gives you money."

For this reason, some of the righteous, when someone came to them seeking charity, would say, "Welcome to one who comes bearing my good deeds to the Hereafter without wage," and would receive him with joy and welcome.

The saying of the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, ﴿Master of the Day of Judgment﴾ is a momentous matter of the articles of faith, for it tells us that the beginning is from God and the end is to God, majestic is His majesty. Since we will all meet God, we must work for this day. Therefore the believer does nothing in his life without God being in his mind, and that He will reckon with him on the Day of Resurrection. But the non-believer does what he does with God absent from his mind, and concerning such people the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿And those who disbelieve, their deeds are like a mirage in a level plain, which the thirsty one thinks is water, until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing, and finds God with him, and He pays him his account in full. And God is swift in reckoning.﴾ (Surah al-Nur, 39).

Thus whoever does something with God absent from his mind will be surprised on the Day of Resurrection that God, blessed and exalted is He, whom he did not have in mind, exists, and that He, majestic is His majesty, is the One who will reckon with him.

And His saying, ﴿Master of the Day of Judgment﴾, is the foundation of the religion, because the one who does not believe in the Hereafter does whatever he wishes. For as long as he believes there is no Hereafter and no reckoning, of what will he be afraid, and for whose sake will he restrain his movement in life?

Indeed the entire religion, with all its acts of obedience and all its method, rests on the fact that there is a reckoning in the Hereafter, and that there is a day on which we all stand before God, glorified and exalted is He, to call the wrongdoer to account and reward the obedient. This is the governing principle in all our acts of faith. For if there were no day on which we are reckoned, why would we pray? Why would we fast? Why would we give charity?

Indeed every movement of the methods of heaven rests on that day from which no one will escape, and for which we must all prepare. God, glorified and exalted is He, has named this day, for the believers, the Day of Supreme Triumph, which makes us bear everything we dislike.

Before we speak of the words of the Truthful, may He be blessed and exalted: ﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾, we must discuss an important matter. There are two kinds of seeing: seeing with the eye, that is, with the eyes, and seeing through faith, that is, with the heart. Each differs from the other. Seeing with the eye means that a thing is in front of you and you see it with your eyes, and there is no matter of faith in this. You do not say, "I believe that I see you in front of me, because you are truly seeing me." As long as you see him, this is certainty. But the seeing of faith means that you believe as if you were seeing what is unseen before you. This seeing is more certain than seeing with the eye, because it is the seeing of faith and of insight. This is a very important matter.

Umar ibn al-Khattab narrated that he said:

"While we were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ one day, there came upon us a man of intensely white clothing and intensely black hair. No trace of travel was seen on him, and none of us knew him. He sat down before the Prophet ﷺ, leaned his knees against his knees, and placed his palms on his thighs. He said: 'O Muhammad, tell me about Islam.' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Islam is that you testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, establish the prayer, give the zakat, fast Ramadan, and make pilgrimage to the House if you are able to reach it.' He said: 'You have spoken truly.' We were amazed that he asked him and then affirmed his answer.

He said: 'Tell me about faith.'

He said: 'That you believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day, and that you believe in predestination, its good and its evil.'

He said: 'You have spoken truly. Tell me about ihsan.' He said: 'That you worship Allah as if you see Him. And if you do not see Him, He sees you.'

He said: 'Tell me about the Hour.'

He said: 'The one asked about it knows no more than the one asking.'

He said: 'Then tell me about its signs.'

He said: 'That the slave-girl gives birth to her mistress, and that you see the barefoot, naked, destitute herders of sheep competing in building tall buildings.'

He said: 'Then he departed, and I remained a while. Then the Prophet ﷺ said to me: "O Umar, do you know who the questioner was?" I said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "That was Jibril. He came to you to teach you your religion."' (1)

The saying of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, "That you worship Allah as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, He sees you," is an explanation of the seeing of faith in the believing soul. When a person believes, he must take all his matters with the vision of faith. So when he reads a verse about Paradise, it is as if he sees the people of Paradise enjoying its bounties, and when he reads a verse about the people of the Fire, his skin shivers, as if he sees the people of the Fire being punished.

One day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw one of his Companions whose name was al-Harith, and said to him:

"How have you risen this morning, O Harith?"

He said: "I have risen a true believer."

The Messenger said: "Consider what you say, for every saying has a reality. What is the reality of your faith?" Al-Harith said: "My soul has turned away from this world, so I have kept my nights awake and my days thirsty. It is as if I look at the Throne of my Lord laid bare, as if I look at the people of Paradise visiting one another in it, and as if I look at the people of the Fire crying out in it." (That is, shouting in it.)

The Prophet said: "O Harith, you have known, so hold fast to it." (2)

For this reason we find that the Truthful, glorified and exalted, when addressing the Messenger ﷺ, says:

﴿Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant?﴾ (Surah al-Fil)

Some orientalists (al-mustashriqun) take this verse in an attempt to attack the Noble Qur'an. The statement of the Exalted, ﴿Have you not considered﴾, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was born in the Year of the Elephant, means that he did not see it, because he was a child of days or months old. They say: if Allah, glorified and exalted, had said "Have you not known," we would say he learned it from someone else. Knowledge is something you acquire yourself or that someone else gives you from his knowledge, that is, someone among mankind teaches you. But Allah, glorified and exalted, said: ﴿Have you not considered﴾.

We say that this is a matter of faith. What the Allah, glorified and exalted, says is a true seeing for the believing person. The Qur'an is speech whose recitation is an act of worship until the Hour is established. The saying of Allah, ﴿Have you not considered﴾, means that the seeing continues for every believer in Allah who reads this verse. Since Allah, blessed and exalted, said ﴿Have you not considered﴾, you see with your faith what your eye is unable to see. This is the seeing of faith, and it is truer than the seeing of the eye, because the eye may deceive its owner, but the believing heart never deceives its owner.

Moreover, there is what they call the third person (ḍamīr al-ghā'ib). If you say, "Zayd has arrived," he is present before you. But if you say, "I met Zayd," it is as if Zayd was absent from you at the moment you said this sentence. You met him, but he is not present with you at the time of the speech.

Thus there is the present, the absent, and the speaker. The absent is the one who is not present or whom we do not see at the time of speaking. The present is the one who is present at the time of speaking. The speaker is the one who speaks. All matters of creed contain no witnessing, but faith in what is unseen to us gives us the seeing of faith, which, as we have said, is stronger than the sight of the eye.

So when Allah, glorified and exalted, says ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾, "Allah" is unseen, ﴿Lord of the worlds﴾ is unseen, ﴿the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful﴾ is unseen, and ﴿Sovereign of the Day of Recompense﴾ is unseen. The linguistic context would require that it be said, "Him we worship." But Allah, glorified and exalted, changed the context and moved it from the absent to the present, and said ﴿You alone we worship﴾. So the unseen turned into the presence of the addressee. He did not say "Him we worship," but said ﴿You alone we worship﴾, and it became a seeing of faithful certainty.

Thus you are in the presence of Allah, glorified and exalted, who has overwhelmed you with blessings, and you see these blessings encompassing you, because He is ﴿Lord of the worlds﴾. He made you feel secure in His decree, because He is ﴿the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful﴾, meaning that His lordship, majestic is He, is not a lordship of tyranny, but is the lordship of ﴿the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful﴾. So if you do not praise Him and believe in Him for the favor of His blessings which you feel and live within, then beware of opposing His method, for He is ﴿Sovereign of the Day of Recompense﴾.

When the Truthful, glorified and exalted, brings His essence to mind with all these attributes, in which are the virtues of divinity, the blessings of lordship, the mercy that erases sins, and the awe of meeting Him on the Day of Resurrection, you have moved from the attributes of the unseen to the presence of witnessing. You have brought to mind the majesty of Allah's divinity and the outpourings of His mercy, His blessings which have no limit, and His sustaining power on the Day of Resurrection.

When you read His saying, exalted is He, ﴿You alone we worship﴾, the expression here conveys exclusivity. That is, if I say to a person, "I will meet you," I may meet him alone, and I may meet him with a group of people. But if I say, "It is you alone I will meet," it means the meeting will be private.

When the Truthful, glorified and exalted, said ﴿You alone we worship﴾, He restricted worship to His noble Essence, because if He had said, "We worship You alone," it would not convey the same meaning, since you might say "We worship You alone" while also worshipping others along with Him. But when you say "You alone we worship," and you place "You alone" first, you have settled the matter that worship is for Allah alone, so no conjunction may be made with it. Worship is submission to Allah, glorified and exalted, through His method: do this and do not do that. For this reason He made the prayer the foundation of worship, and prostration is the utmost of submission to Allah, because you bring your face, which is the most honorable thing in you, and place it on the ground at the place of the feet. This is the utmost submission to Allah, and it is performed before all the people in the prayer, to announce your submission to Allah before all mankind.

In worship the rich and the poor, the great and the small are equal, so that each of us drives out pride and arrogance from his heart before all the people. Thus the Truthful, majestic is He, makes His servants equal in submission to Him and in announcing this submission. The saying of the Truthful, glorified and exalted, ﴿You alone we worship﴾ negates worship of other than Allah, meaning we do not worship other than Allah and never conjoin anything with Him. Thus "You alone we worship" gives the specification of worship to Allah alone, there is no god besides Him and no one worshipped other than Him. We must pay attention to the saying of the blessed and exalted:

﴿Had there been within the heavens and the earth gods other than Allah, they would have been ruined. So exalted is Allah, Lord of the Throne, above what they describe﴾ (Surah al-Anbiya', 22).

Thus, when we say "All praise is due to Allah," we bring to mind the causes of praise, which are the apparent and hidden blessings of Allah. When we say "Lord of the worlds," we bring to mind the blessings of lordship over His creation and His subjugation of the universe. When we bring to mind "the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful," we bring to mind mercy, forgiveness, repaying evil with good, and the opening of the door of repentance. When we bring to mind "Sovereign of the Day of Recompense," we bring to mind the Day of Reckoning and how Allah, blessed and exalted, will recompense you for your deeds. If we bring all this to mind, we say "You alone we worship," meaning we worship Allah alone. Thus we know what is required of us, which is worship.

Here we pause briefly to speak about what they call in language "the cause and the effect." If your son wants to pass the examination, he must study, and the cause of studying is success. So it is as if success was born in my mind first, with all the advantages it brings me, a secure future, and other things I desire and strive for.

So the motive comes before the reality, meaning you first brought success to mind, and afterward you studied to make success a real fact. If you want, for example, to travel to a certain place, the car is one cause that achieves what you want, and cutting across the road is another cause. But the motive that made me leave my house, get into the car, and cross the road is that I want to travel to Alexandria, for example. The motive here, which is reaching Alexandria, is what existed in my mind first, and then I did everything I did to achieve it.

Allah, glorified and exalted, created us in life so that we worship Him, in confirmation of the saying of the blessed and exalted:

﴿I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me﴾ (Surah al-Dhariyat, 56).

So the cause of creation is worship, and creation was completed so that worship would be realized and become a fact. But "cause and effect" does not apply to the acts of Allah, glorified and exalted. We say there is no cause that returns to Allah, majestic is He, with benefit, because Allah, blessed and exalted, is free of need of the worlds. But the cause returns to creation with benefit. So Allah, glorified and exalted, created us to worship Him, but the cause of creation is not that this worship would add anything to His dominion. Rather our worship returns to us with good in this world and the Hereafter.

The acts of Allah are not subject to causation, and the one commanded to worship is the one who will benefit from it.

But is worship sitting in the mosques and glorifying Allah, or is it a method that encompasses all of life, in your home, in your work, and in your striving upon the earth? If Allah, glorified and exalted, wanted from His servants only prayer and glorification, He would not have created them with free choice; rather He would have created them compelled to His worship, as He created everything other than mankind and jinn. And Allah, blessed and exalted, has the attribute of compulsion. From here, He is able to make whomever He wills compelled to His worship, in confirmation of the saying of the majestic:

﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief that they do not believe. If We willed, We could send down upon them from the heaven a sign, so their necks would remain bowed before it﴾ (Surah al-Shu'ara', 3–4).

So if Allah wanted to subject us to His method by compulsion, no one could deviate from His obedience. Allah has given us the proof of this, in that in our bodies and in the events of this world there is what we are compelled to. The body is compelled to Allah in many things. The heart beats and stops by the command of Allah without any will from us. The stomach digests food and we know nothing of it. The circulation of blood in our bodies has no will of ours in it. Many things in the human body are all compelled to Allah, glorified and exalted, and our will has no part in their working. And what befalls me in the events of worldly life is something I am compelled in. I cannot prevent it from happening. I cannot prevent a car from striking me, nor an airplane from burning me, nor anything that befalls me of the decrees of Allah in this world.

So the realm of my choice in life is limited. I cannot control the day of my birth, nor who my father is and who my mother is, nor my form: whether I am tall or short, handsome or ugly, or otherwise. So the realm of choice in life is the method, that...

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 1, verse 6:

After you have believed in Allah, glorified and exalted be He, as your God and Lord, and have called to mind the bounty of divinity, the blessings of lordship, and the overflowing mercy of Allah upon His creation, and you have declared that there is no god but Allah. Your saying "You alone do we worship" means that worship belongs to Allah, blessed and exalted is He: we do not associate anything with Him, and we worship none but Him. And you have declared that you will seek help from Allah alone by your saying "You alone do we ask for help." Thus you have become one of the servants of Allah. Allah, glorified and exalted be He, teaches you the supplication that every believer desires. And since you are among the servants of Allah, Allah, majestic in His majesty, will respond to you, in confirmation of His saying, glorified be He:

﴿And when My servants ask you concerning Me, indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me. So let them respond to Me and believe in Me that they may be guided.﴾ (Surat al-Baqarah, 186)

The believer never seeks this world. Why? Because the true life of man is in the Hereafter, where there is everlasting life and bliss that never leaves you and that you never leave. So the believer does not ask, for example, that Allah grant him much wealth, or that he own a building, for example, because he knows that all of this is temporary and fleeting. Rather, he asks for that which saves him from the Fire and brings him to Paradise.

It is among the mercy of Allah, blessed and exalted is He, that He has taught us what to ask for, and this necessitates praising Allah. The first thing the believer asks for is guidance and the straight path: ﴿Guide us to the straight path.﴾

Guidance is of two kinds: guidance of indication (hidayat al-dalalah) and guidance of assistance (hidayat al-ma'unah). The guidance of indication is for all people, and the guidance of assistance is for believers only, those who follow the method of Allah. Allah, glorified and exalted be He, gave all His servants the guidance of indication, meaning He pointed them to the path of good and made it clear to them. So whoever wishes to follow the path of good follows it, and whoever wishes not to follow it, Allah leaves him to what he wills.

This general guidance is the foundation of the conveyance of the message from Allah. Allah, blessed and exalted is He, has made clear to us in His method what to do and what not to do, what pleases Him and what angers Him. He has clarified for us the path that we follow in order to be guided. And the path which, if we took it, would bring upon us the wrath and anger of Allah. But is it the case that everyone to whom Allah, glorified and exalted be He, has shown the path of guidance is guided? We say no. Read His saying, majestic be His majesty:

﴿As for Thamud, We guided them, but they preferred blindness over guidance, so the seizure of the humiliating punishment took them for what they used to earn.﴾ (Surat Fussilat, 17)

So there are those who do not take the path of guidance by the choice that Allah gave them. Had Allah, glorified and exalted be He, willed that we all be guided, not one of His creatures could have gone against His will. But He, majestic in His majesty, created us as choosers, so that we come to Him out of love and desire, rather than compelling us to obey. What happens to those who follow the path of guidance, and to those who do not follow it and oppose the legislated will of Allah in His creation?

﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and grants them their piety.﴾ (Surat Muhammad, 17)

That is, whoever takes the path of guidance, Allah helps him to it, and increases him in piety and love for the religion. As for those who, when guidance comes to them, turn away from the method of Allah and oppose it, then Allah, blessed and exalted is He, forsakes them and leaves them in their misguidance. Read His saying, exalted be He:

﴿And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful, We appoint for him a devil, and he is to him a companion.﴾ (Surat al-Zukhruf, 36)

Allah, glorified and exalted be He, has explained to us those who are deprived of the guidance of assistance in faith, and they are three, as He has made them known to us in the Noble Qur'an:

﴿That is because they preferred the worldly life over the Hereafter, and that Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.﴾ (Surat al-Nahl, 107)

﴿That is more suitable that they would give testimony in its proper form, or fear that oaths would be repeated after their oaths. And fear Allah and listen. And Allah does not guide the defiant people.﴾ (Surat al-Ma'idah, 108)

﴿Have you not considered the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord, because Allah had given him kingship? When Abraham said, "My Lord is the one who gives life and causes death," he said, "I give life and cause death." Abraham said, "Indeed, Allah brings the sun from the east, so bring it from the west." So the one who disbelieved was overwhelmed. And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾ (Surat al-Baqarah, 258)

So those barred from the guidance of Allah in assistance toward faith are the disbelievers, the defiant, and the wrongdoers. The Truthful, glorified and exalted be He, says: ﴿Guide us to the straight path.﴾ What is the path? It is the route leading to the goal. And why is it specified as the straight path? Because Allah, glorified and exalted be He, has set for us in His method the straight path, and it is the shortest route to achieving the goal. The shortest path between two points is the straight line. Therefore, if you intend a place, the shortest way you can take is the route that has no crookedness, but is perfectly straight.

Do not imagine that deviation from the straight path begins with a large crookedness. Rather, it begins with a very small crookedness, but it ends in a great distance.

It suffices that you observe the railway tracks. When the train begins to take a route other than the one it was following, it at first deviates only by a few millimeters. That is, the first switch is very narrow, and the further you go, the wider the difference becomes and keeps widening. So that at the end you find that the road you traveled on is distant from the first road by tens of kilometers, and perhaps hundreds of kilometers. Thus, any deviation, however slight, takes you far from the straight path. Therefore the supplication "Guide us to the straight path" means the path in which there is no crookedness, even by a few millimeters, the path in which there is no violation that distances us from the straight path of Allah.

For this reason the believing person asks Allah, glorified and exalted be He, to guide him to the shortest routes to reach the goal. And what is the goal? It is Paradise and bliss in the Hereafter. Therefore we say: O Lord, guide us and help us to follow the straight path, which is the path of the method, so that it may bring us to Paradise without any crookedness that distances us from it.

Allah, glorified and exalted be He, has said in a Hadith Qudsi that when the servant says, "Guide us to the straight path," He, majestic in His majesty, says: "This is for My servant, and My servant shall have what he asks."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 1, verse 7:

The Exalted, blessed and high is He, says: ﴿The path of those upon whom You have bestowed favour﴾. What is the meaning of "those upon whom You have bestowed favour"?.. Read the noble verse:

﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger – those are with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favour of the prophets, the steadfast lovers of truth (al-siddiqin), the martyrs and the righteous. And excellent are those as companions.﴾ (Surat al-Nisa', 69)

When you recite this noble verse, you are asking Allah, blessed and exalted, that you be with the prophets, the siddiqin, the martyrs and the righteous. That is, you are asking Allah, Majestic in His majesty, to make you follow the same path that these have followed, so that you may be with them in the Hereafter. It is as if you are asking for a high rank in Paradise, because everyone we have mentioned has a lofty station in the Garden of Bliss. Thus, the request to Allah, glory be to Him, is that He make you travel the path that has no crookedness, and that brings you, in the quickest time, to a high rank in the Hereafter.

When we know that Allah, glory be to Him, said: (This is for My servant, and My servant shall have what he asks), you know that the response gives you a high life in the Hereafter and enjoyment of Allah's bounty, not by the capacities of humans as happens in this world, but by the power of Allah, blessed and exalted. And if the blessings of this world cannot be counted or enumerated, how then will be the blessings of the Hereafter? Allah, glory be to Him, has said of them:

﴿For them therein is whatever they wish, and with Us is more.﴾ (Surat Qaf, 35)

That is, not everything you ask for will be found before you merely by its occurring to your mind; rather, however much you ask for blessings and however much you wish, Allah, Majestic in His majesty, has more. Therefore He gives you everything you wish and adds to it what you did not ask for and do not know of blessings. This is only an illustration, so that Allah, blessed and exalted, may bring the image of bliss close to our minds; but in Paradise is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived.

Since meanings must first exist in the mind and then comes the word that expresses them, everything we do not know has no words in our language that express it. For instance, we did not know the name "television" until it was invented and acquired a defined concept, just as we did not know the name "airplane" before it was invented. Thing first exists, and then the word expressing it is assigned. Therefore the language academies of the world convene from time to time to assign names to new things that have been invented and whose function has become known.

Since that is the linguistic rule, there are no words in human language that express the bliss that the people of Paradise will live in, because no eye has seen it, no ear has heard of it, and it has not occurred to the heart. Therefore everything we read in the Noble Qur'an only brings the image close to us, but does not give us the reality of what exists. Accordingly, when Allah, glory be to Him, speaks of Paradise in the Noble Qur'an, He says:

﴿The likeness of the Garden which the righteous are promised: in it are rivers of water unaltered, and rivers of milk whose taste does not change, and rivers of wine, delicious to drinkers, and rivers of purified honey. For them therein is every fruit, and forgiveness from their Lord. Are they like one who abides in the Fire and is given boiling water to drink, which cuts their intestines?﴾ (Surat Muhammad, 15)

That is, this is not the reality of Paradise but only a likeness to bring that close to minds, because there are no words in human languages that can give us the reality of what is in Paradise.

And His saying, ﴿not of those who have earned anger﴾: that is, not of those whom You, O Lord, have been angry with, from among those who disobeyed, and from whom You have withheld the guidance of help. Those who knew the method and opposed it and committed everything Allah had forbidden, so they deserved His anger.

The meaning of "not those who have earned anger" is: O Lord, do not facilitate for us the path by which we would deserve Your anger, as those deserved it who altered and changed the method of Allah in order to take temporal authority in the life of this world and to devour people's wealth falsely.

The phrase "those who have earned anger" occurs in the Noble Qur'an in His saying:

﴿Say: Shall I inform you of something worse than that as a recompense from Allah? Those whom Allah has cursed and with whom He became angry and made of them apes and swine, and who worshipped the Taghut. Those are worse in position and further astray from the right way.﴾ (Surat al-Ma'idah, 60)

These verses were revealed concerning the Children of Israel.

And the saying of Allah, ﴿nor of those who are astray﴾: there is the one who is astray (al-dall) and the one who misleads (al-mudill). The one who is astray is he who has lost the way, adopting a method other than the method of Allah, and walking in error far from guidance and the religion of Allah. It is said "he lost the way" meaning he walked in it while not knowing the path to what he wished to reach. That is, he wandered in this world and became a friend of Satan and moved far from the straight path of Allah. This is the one who is astray. But the misleader is one who is not content with having turned away from the method of Allah and walking through life without guidance, but rather tries to take others into error. He entices people toward disbelief, not following the method, and turning away from the path of Allah. Every one of the disobedient comes on the Day of Resurrection carrying his own sins, except the misleader, who carries his own sins and the sins of those he misled, in confirmation of His saying, glory be to Him:

﴿That they may bear their burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection, and of the burdens of those whom they mislead without knowledge. Unquestionably, evil is that which they bear.﴾ (Surat al-Nahl, 25)

That is, when you recite al-Fatihah you seek refuge in Allah from being among those who went astray. But the Exalted, blessed and high is He, did not mention the misleaders here. We say that in order to be a misleader you must first be astray. So seeking refuge from straying here includes both. For as long as you have sought refuge from being astray, you will never be a misleader.
